annotations.text:
CHOSE A — Inline chips, crop rail.

A citation is only worth anything if you can tell which claim it holds up, and A is the only direction where that binding cannot be misread — the path sits inside the sentence, and the rail gives the crop enough room to actually be read.

B is prettier until a claim carries three citations. C decouples claim from proof, which is the one failure this screen exists to prevent.

The amber block in the answer is deliberate, not filler. An unresolved or ambiguous ref is a fact about the corpus, so the answer states what it could not close and hands it to the review queue, rather than quietly picking a candidate. Same amber the queue uses for model-derived and ambiguous.

The plan panel is the SPEC 6 planning step made visible: the question restated as sub-queries with an explicit parallel batch structure, batch 2 showing its dependency on batch 1. This is what streams to the user as "working on" before any tool runs.
